== Account summary ==
Backup candidate for Customer Reference Program (EMEA). Insurance org w/ heavy compliance posture. Interest in Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated in EU region.

Primary themes so far: early security review questions, data residency constraints, and marketing/public reference risk assessment.

== Firmographics / fit ==
- Region: EMEA (customer team in EU; procurement + risk functions centralized)
- Workload: internal claims + underwriting assistant (summaries of adjuster notes, policy docs, and customer communications). Also exploring contact-center “agent assist” style workflows.
- Why Redwood: wants predictable latency + ability to keep traffic in-region; prefers “same API across environments” so they can start with dedicated and migrate to private/VPC if needed.

== Deployment + technical notes (early) ==
- Stated deployment requirement: EU-only processing, preference for Frankfurt. Asked whether Redwood can commit to regional pinning at the account level and how failover works (must not failover to US regions).
- VPC/Private: wants customer-managed networking; asked if outbound internet egress can be restricted.
- Key management: asked for options (customer-managed keys / KMS integration). Wants clear statement on key ownership and access controls.
- Audit logging: wants detailed audit log fields + export cadence. (They referenced internal audit requirements; likely will ask for sample schema.)
- Retention: wants retention controls and confirmation of log retention vs payload retention.

== Security / compliance notes ==
- Procurement/risk asked for: SOC 2 report, ISO cert status, subprocessor list, DPA posture (GDPR), incident response overview.
- Specific question: “Do you process prompts/outputs outside the EU for ops/support?” They want the answer to be “no” for production data.
- SSO/SAML likely required for Console access (if they proceed).

== Public reference / case study risk assessment ==
- Very cautious on marketing exposure.
- Initial read: high likelihood they will only approve anonymized participation (reference call or case study as “Large EU insurer”) and may decline logo usage entirely.
- Quotes: if any, must be pre-approved and attributed to a comms-approved spokesperson (legal + brand team sign-off). No engineering staff quotes without comms review.
- Architecture detail: may allow high-level architecture (VPC + audit logging + KMS) but will restrict anything that reveals internal systems or region/vendor specifics.

== Activity timeline ==
- 2025-05-30: Account created in HubSpot as EMEA backup reference candidate (source: internal reference program target list discussion).
- 2025-06-14: Outreach from Hannah Schmitt re: reference program participation. Customer replied: open to discussion, but flagged EU data residency and publicity limits (anonymized story only).
- 2025-06-18: Internal note: route to SE (Simran) for residency/KMS/audit log deep dive; do not push logo/quote release until constraints confirmed.

== Next steps (proposed) ==
- Security deep dive (SE + customer risk/security): EU region pinning + failover policy, VPC options, KMS/key access model, audit log export format, retention controls.
- After security alignment: soft-ask for reference participation as either:
  (1) reference-call-only (anonymized), or
  (2) public case study without logo, with generic attribution + vetted metrics.

== Internal notes ==
- Treat as “backup” reference only until we confirm: (a) EU-only routing commitment, (b) willingness to do any customer advocacy.
- If they require strict no-publicity, could still be useful for 1:1 reference calls under NDA with tight topic boundaries.
- If we get traction, loop in Legal early (Sofia Mendes / Michael Grant) before sending any release language.
